title: Multi-Table INNER, LEFT, FULL Joins & CTEs
summary: Compose multi-table joins safely preserving unmatched left records without accidentally converting LEFT JOINs into INNER JOINs.
learningObjectives: Place optional table filters inside `ON` vs `WHERE` cleanly to protect LEFT JOIN unmatched rows
Break nested query complexity into readable step-by-step Common Table Expressions (`WITH` clauses)
prerequisiteConcepts: Basic SELECT and foreign key modeling

sections.heading: 1. Join Cardinality, Outer Join Pitfalls & CTE Clarity
sections.content:
Whenever joining tables, track join cardinality carefully: joining 1 Customer to 5 Orders yields 5 rows—joining 5 Orders AND 3 Support Tickets directly multiplies into 15 duplicated fanout rows (`5 x 3` Cartesian trap!), inflating `SUM(order_total)` 3x! Aggregating separate pre-computed **Common Table Expressions (CTEs)** before joining eliminates fanout distortion completely.

Second classic bug: placing right-table conditions like `WHERE o.status = 'paid'` after a `LEFT JOIN orders o` destroys unmatched NULL customers, quietly converting `LEFT JOIN` back to an `INNER JOIN`! Put right-table match filters inside the `LEFT JOIN ... ON` condition whenever preserving unmatched left entities.

codeExamples.code:
[Safe Left Join Filter]      FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id AND o.status = 'paid'
                             -> Unmatched users stay cleanly in result with o.* = NULL!
[Buggy Left Join Filter]     FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id WHERE o.status = 'paid'
                             -> NULL status rows get DROPPED by WHERE!
codeExamples.explanation: Right-side filter placement decides whether unmatched parent records survive cleanly or get silently discarded.

keyPoints: Aggregate child branches separately inside `WITH` CTEs before joining two independent `1-to-many` tables!
Avoid implicit old comma joins (`FROM a, b`) that risk accidental full Cartesian products.
commonMistakes: Computing `SUM(orders.amount)` while simultaneously joining `order_line_items`, inflating every order total by its line-item count!

sections.heading: 2. Anti-Fanout CTE Pipeline
sections.content: Look how pre-aggregating inside two clean CTEs guarantees accurate, readable customer metrics with zero duplication risk.

codeExamples.code:
WITH customer_spend AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(total_cents) AS total_cents
  FROM orders
  WHERE status = 'paid'
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_tickets AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS open_tickets
  FROM support_tickets
  WHERE status = 'open'
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.full_name,
  COALESCE(s.order_count, 0) AS orders,
  COALESCE(s.total_cents, 0) AS lifetime_spend_cents,
  COALESCE(t.open_tickets, 0) AS open_tickets
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN customer_spend s ON c.id = s.customer_id
LEFT JOIN customer_tickets t ON c.id = t.customer_id;
codeExamples.explanation: Aggregating `orders` and `tickets` in separate `1-row-per-customer` CTEs ensures joining both onto `customers` creates zero row multiplication.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Accurate per-customer lifetime spend & ticket counts preserving customers with zero orders

keyPoints: CTEs turn fragile nested subqueries into self-documenting sequential transformations.
commonMistakes: Joining `1-to-Many-A` AND `1-to-Many-B` straight onto a root table prior to aggregating.

exercises.title: Fix Fanout & Outer Join Bug in Sales Query
exercises.objective: Repair a query dropping inactive customers and inflating totals.
exercises.description: Fix: `SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id), COUNT(t.id) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id=o.cid LEFT JOIN tickets t ON c.id=t.cid WHERE o.status='paid' GROUP BY c.id, c.name;`
instructions: Preserve customers having zero orders cleanly.
Prevent `orders × tickets` Cartesian count inflation via separate CTEs.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why should you avoid joining two separate `1-to-Many` tables (`orders` and `refunds`) directly onto `customers` before aggregating?

options.text: It triggers a cross-product fanout between a customer's orders and refunds, wildly inflating SUM/COUNT totals
PostgreSQL throws syntax error on joining three tables
LEFT JOIN ignores foreign keys after 2 tables

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Pre-aggregating per parent key in CTEs prevents cross-branch multiplicative row duplication.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: When joining `students LEFT JOIN submissions` and wanting ALL students—plus ONLY submissions with `score >= 90`—where should `s.score >= 90` be placed?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Putting it in `WHERE` filters out NULL unmatched students.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What does `COALESCE(val, 0)` accomplish cleanly alongside a `LEFT JOIN`?

options.text: Replaces missing unmatched NULL metrics gracefully with `0` for reporting and safe arithmetic

knowledgeChecks.explanation: `COALESCE` substitutes explicit defaults whenever expressions evaluate to NULL.

recap: You eliminated silent outer-join regressions and prevented multiplicative join fanout via structured CTEs.
